title: Add files, folders and pictures in {name}: drop, pick or paste
description: Drop PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV or text files and pictures on {name}’s box, pick them with +, or paste them. What it reads, what it keeps, and folders.
works: Every browser. A folder is changed where it is in Chrome and Edge, on a computer.
answer: Drop them on the box, or press + beside it, then write what you want done with them and send. {name} reads PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV and text files, and shows pictures to brains that can see. Each file stays in the project, to use again.
pane.title: A file shared with a request, answered in {name}
demo.asked: Sum up what the team says in this survey, in four points, and what they ask for most.
demo.answer:
Here is what the 24 answers say:

1. **The new schedule works**: most find Thursday’s meeting shorter and clearer.
2. **Onboarding is too fast**: newcomers want a written guide for their first week.
3. **Tools are scattered**: files live in three places, and people lose time looking.
4. **Recognition matters**: several ask for wins to be shared more often.

What they ask for most: **one place for the team’s files**, named in 15 of the 24 answers.
steps: Drag files from your desktop or a folder onto the box: {drop} shows where they go.
Or press + beside the box, then {attach} if it opens a menu, and choose them.
To add a picture you copied, or a screenshot, paste it in the box: Ctrl and V, or ⌘ and V on a Mac.
Each file shows above the box, {reading} at first, then its pages or {picture}. Its × takes it off before you send.
Write what you want done with them, and send: sum it up, compare them, fill this form from that letter.
parts: Drop a folder on the conversation, and {name} asks {work} In Chrome and Edge, on a computer, it finds, reads and changes its files where they are, showing you each change first. In other browsers it works on a copy, and {save} gives you what changed. Once you have used one, + has {folder}.
Where the browser allows it, + has {capture}: {name} takes a picture of a window or of your screen, and adds it as it would a file.
good: Each file is kept in the project, on this device. In a later task, type @ in the box and part of its name to point at it again.
The brain reads the files’ text. With a brain in the cloud, it goes there with your request: see {sees}.
A scan, or a picture of a page, has no text to read: brains that can see are shown it instead.
With a spreadsheet, {name} offers to work out the figures with a program, rather than guess them.
fixes: A file over 100 MB can’t go in. Split it, or export the part you need. For many files, drop their folder instead.
{name} doesn’t read that kind of file yet. Save it as a PDF or a text file first, from the app that made it.
The file holds pictures of pages, not text. A brain that can see reads them: most brains in the cloud can.
